title: BTY arXiv:2603.21490 read: new best CLASSICAL zero-free record A = 4.896 (improved 4.8594) — verified at statement+mechanism level; contributes NOTHING to the residual face (contained in the [Z78T] cover for all t > 5.112; face starts at tPT2 = 3.0e12 where the BTY boundary is 0.992891); not adopted
body: Read and verified (statement + mechanism level, sufficient because of the zero-contribution computation below) Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang, 'Zero-free regions inspired by work of Heath-Brown', arXiv 2603.21490 v1 (March 2026; tarball sha256 d59e58cbf9ec4e74448b7cc3a856564b2a94cdbf67a95a16a21420809dd42489 on file in tmp/b6audit/bty/; 1,387-line TeX). STATEMENT (Thm 1.1, verified from source): for t >= 3, zeta(sigma+it) != 0 in sigma > 1 - 1/(4.896 log t) — the best explicit CLASSICAL (log-width) record: improves Mossinghoff 5.559 (lineage: de la Valle Poussin 1899 ... Ford 2002 8.463, Mossinghoff 2022 5.559). Thm 1.2 (from the Yang thesis constants): 4.8594. MECHANISM (read and checked): generalized zero-detector explicit formula (valid inside the strip, Hadamard-product form with Laplace transform F of a compactly supported weight); nonnegative trigonometric polynomial P(theta) = sum a_k cos(k theta), a_k > 0, a_1 > a_0 (generalizing 3 + 4cos + cos 2); Stechkin PAIR-positivity condition Re F(s-rho) + Re F(s-(1-rho-bar)) >= 0; Kadiri-style inductive deepening; test function f(u) = eta w(eta u) sum_m kappa_m e^{-(2sigma-1) m u} = Heath-Brown's w (theta-family, Lemma 7.1 of his 1992 paper) tensor a 7-term discrete L-inf[0,1] approximant of the limiting sigmoid 1/(1+e^{-u}) with kappa = [1, -851/859, 780/859, -525/859, 171/859, 28/859, -29/859] (computationally chosen, rationalized). VERIFIED NUMERICS: sum(kappa) = 433/859, giving the paper's efficiency constant c = 859/433 = 1.98383... (ideal limit c = 2: (a_1 F(0) - a_0 F(-eta))/f(0) = (c+O(eta))(a_1 W(0) - a_0 W(-1))/(eta w(0)); c/2 = 0.99192, loss 0.808% < 1% = the paper's 'within one percent' claim, re-derived). The optimized range is restricted to 3 <= t <= exp(76.47) — zeros JUST ABOVE the Platt-H = 3e12 verified plateau are the hardest; above that, explicit Littlewood (21.233, thesis 19.62) covers the remainder. Zero-free regions quoted (Yang): 1 - loglog t/(21.233 log t) (thesis 19.62); (Bellotti): 1 - 1/(53.989 (log t)^{2/3}(loglog t)^{1/3}) (thesis 51.34); Bbound sharper than Ybound only for t > exp(482036). ZERO-CONTRIBUTION PROOF (the decisive computation): the BTY boundary 1 - 1/(4.896 log t) equals the [Z78T] boundary 0.874817065 at t = exp(1/(4.896 * 0.125182935)) = 5.112 and is strictly LARGER (weaker) for all t > 5.112; at the face height tPT2 = 3,000,175,332,800 the BTY boundary is 0.992891 while the residual face hOffT spans sigma in [0.125182935, 0.874817065] — DISJOINT. The only t-interval where the BTY region sticks out left of [Z78T] is t in [3, 5.112] (boundary 0.814..0.8748), five orders of magnitude below the face and inside the computationally verified plateau in any case. CONSEQUENCE: BTY is a genuine classical-frontier record but is subsumed by the [Z78T] half-plane exactly where our face lives; it is NOT adopted and changes no in-tree constant. INTELLIGENCE: (a) the classical direction is at decaying returns by the authors' own stabilization footnote — the induction limits, no path to 1/2 in that family; (b) both the BTY group and the tracker board and this program all anchor to the same Platt 3e12 plateau as the natural 'hard edge'; (c) their P(theta) cosine-detector nonnegativity machinery is the same zero-pair-isolation device family as our S4Strip/WinCount atoms, aimed at the 1 - A/log t boundary instead of a fixed theta. No RH claim; [Z78T] remains the frontier. QUEUE: the two remaining 0138 items (de Bruijn-Newman constant Lean composition, 2026-10-08; Mori 0.874957020 Zenodo certificate) are ecosystem/provenance-pattern only and will be logged in discovery 0140 if anything changes the footing analysis.
